title: Enterprise AI Implementation Playbook
description: A practical rollout playbook for teams: pilot selection, governance, measurement, and scaling AI safely across the organization.

data.text: Enterprise AI success is rarely a tooling problem. It is usually an implementation problem: unclear ownership, weak governance, no quality metrics, and no adoption plan. This playbook helps teams roll out AI in a structured way.

items: Pick 2-3 pilot workflows with clear ROI and low regulatory risk.
Define policy, data controls, and approval boundaries before launch.
Train pilot users on prompt quality and verification habits.
Measure outcomes: time saved, quality score, incident rate.
Scale only successful pilots with documented playbooks.

rows: Defines business goals and adoption mandate
Coaching and weekly workflow quality review

data.caption: Successful enterprise rollout is a governance-and-learning loop, not a one-time launch.

data.title: Implementation success factors
points: Start with measurable pilots, not company-wide rollout
Define governance and data policy early
Invest in user training and workflow documentation
Track both productivity gains and risk incidents
Scale proven patterns, retire weak pilots quickly

cards.title: Pilot
cards.description: 2-3 workflows, clear ROI, low regulatory risk. Goal: prove value and learn what breaks.

cards.title: Stabilize
cards.description: Document playbooks, train users, define quality metrics. Goal: make success repeatable.

cards.title: Scale
cards.description: Expand to more teams, add advanced features, tighten governance. Goal: multiply proven value safely.

data.title: Enterprise rollout example
data.content:
A 500-person SaaS company rolled out AI in three phases over 9 months.

Phase 1 (Pilot, 60 days):
- Selected workflows: support ticket summarization, sales email drafting, internal search
- Defined policy: no customer PII in prompts, all outputs reviewed before sending
- Trained 25 pilot users
- Result: 30% time savings, 2 minor incidents (both caught by review)

Phase 2 (Stabilize, 90 days):
- Documented playbooks for each workflow
- Added quality scorecards and weekly review meetings
- Expanded to 100 users
- Result: 35% time savings, 0 incidents

Phase 3 (Scale, 90 days):
- Rolled out to all customer-facing teams
- Added advanced guardrails and custom model access
- Result: 40% time savings, enterprise-wide adoption

data.title: Compliance reminder
data.text: Before any enterprise rollout, check data residency requirements, industry regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2), and internal security policies. A pilot that violates compliance can create bigger problems than it solves.

data.title: Enterprise scaling example
data.content:
A retail company scaled AI from 1 pilot to 200 users in 6 months.

What went well:
- Started with support ticket summarization (low risk, high volume)
- Trained a champion in each department
- Tracked time savings weekly

What went wrong:
- Skipped data classification for one workflow — customer PII ended up in prompts
- Did not update policy when new tools were adopted — shadow IT grew
- Scaled before measuring pilot success — some teams reverted to old workflows

Lesson: Scale only workflows that passed the pilot, and update policy before adding new tools.

data.title: Warning
data.text: The fastest way to kill an AI program is to scale weak pilots. A failed pilot that gets company-wide attention creates resistance that takes months to overcome. Retire weak pilots quickly and celebrate the ones that work.
